Mechanic.d: A game loop from mechanics.json (layer 2 of the Roblox -> web transfer analysis: transferable, not protectable).

Skin.d: A layer-1 theme or meme from mechanics.json (brainrot, skibidi...). Tracked and crossed with mechanics, never ranked.

Sub-category.d: A finer family inside a mechanic, from the 'sub' entries of mechanics.json. Applied only to games already tagged with the mechanic; 'other' when no sub-keyword matches. For reading, never for ranking.

Game.d: Game title as stored in the snapshot (Roblox name, or web page title).

Creator.d: Roblox creator (user or group) that owns the universe.

Developer.d: Studio credited by the web platform (CrazyGames 'developer', Poki JSON-LD author).

CCU.d: Concurrent users: players online in the game (Roblox 'playing'), as the DAY MEAN of the day's readings — the intraday samples at 08:17 and 14:17 UTC and the snapshot's own reading at 20:17 UTC — so the hour of day cannot move it. A day with a single reading is that reading.
CCU.f: mean of the day's readings of playing (games.roblox.com), snapshot included

Roblox CCU.d: Pooled players of the mechanic: sum of the CCU (day means) of its games that are in this week's sampling frame and above the mechanic's player floor (min_ccu in mechanics.json).
Roblox CCU.f: sum(CCU) over tagged games in FRAME_SORTS with CCU >= min_ccu

Players.d: Same as CCU, summed over the games of the row.

ΔCCU.d: Change of CCU since the previous snapshot compared, in percent. A ratio, so not scaled to 7 days.

Visits/7d.d: Visits gained since the previous snapshot, scaled to 7 days. Roblox counts every server join as a visit, so figures are large; unlike CCU this integrates the whole period and does not depend on the sampling hour.
Visits/7d.f: (visits_now - visits_prev) x 7 / days between the two snapshots

Momentum.d: This period's visit pace compared with the game's lifetime average pace. Above 1 the game is accelerating, below 1 it is fading.

Age.d: Days since the game was created (Roblox 'created') or published (CrazyGames 'addedOn', Poki 'datePublished').

Like ratio.d: Share of positive votes on Roblox.

Server size.d: Maximum players per Roblox server (maxPlayers). A small server hints at a loop that needs few other players, i.e. easier to translate to solo web.

Genre.d: Roblox's official genre pair (genre_l1 / genre_l2), declared by the creator and enforced by Roblox. A free cross-check of the keyword taxonomy.

Official genre.d: Same as Genre, used as a grouping key.

Mechanics.d: Mechanic tags derived from the name (Roblox) or slug + title (web) with the keywords of mechanics.json; a Roblox game no keyword caught falls back to the lane its official genre maps to (see Tag source). Computed when the report is built, never stored.

Tag source.d: How a Roblox game got its lane: 'name' when a keyword matched its title (the loop was read), 'genre' when no keyword matched and Roblox's official genre placed it (the creator's declaration, coarser). Dashed chips and this column mark the second case; each lane also states the share of its players that came in via genre.

Sub-categories.d: Sub-category tags inside each of the game's mechanics (see Sub-category).

Skins.d: Skin tags derived from the name / slug with the skin keywords of mechanics.json.

Social cues.d: Cue families found in the Roblox description: PvP (players act against players), co-op / social, solo. Keyword-based and display-only.

Sorts.d: Roblox discovery sorts the game appears in this week, with its rank. The four frame sorts drive pooled figures; extra sorts (top-earning, top-rated...) are flags.

Rank change.d: Best rank among frame sorts now minus best rank in the previous snapshot. Negative = climbed.

IPs.d: Distinct creators with a game of the mechanic above the floor. The propagation signal: one creator shipping three variants is a franchise, several creators is a genre spreading.
IPs.f: count of distinct creator names among games above min_ccu

Creators.d: Distinct creators among the games of the row.

New IPs.d: Creators above the floor this week that were not above it in the previous snapshot.

Top share.d: Share of the mechanic's pooled CCU held by its single biggest game. Above 60 % the report warns: one hit is not a genre.
Top share.f: CCU of the biggest game / Roblox CCU of the mechanic

New <28d.d: Games of the mechanic (above the floor) listed in Roblox's Up-and-Coming sort, which Roblox describes as experiences published within the last 28 days.

Games.d: Number of games in the row.

Web supply.d: Games in the FULL Poki + CrazyGames sitemap catalogue whose slug matches the entry's web keywords. Counted over the catalogue, never over the watchlist.
Web supply.f: count of catalogue slugs matched by web_kw minus web_exclude

Δsupply.d: Web supply now minus web supply in the previous snapshot, with today's keywords on both catalogues.

Tracked.d: Watchlist games (pages actually read this snapshot) matching the entry. The sample the vote velocity comes from; not a measure of supply.

Votes.d: Cumulative vote count shown by the platform (Poki 'votes', CrazyGames 'ratingCount'). Worthless in absolute terms; CrazyGames' count can decrease from one day to the next.

Votes/7d.d: Votes gained by tracked games present in both snapshots, scaled to 7 days. 'n' is the number of games contributing.

Tech.d: Engine reported by CrazyGames (Unity WebGL, HTML5, ...). Not exposed by Poki.

Category.d: The platform's own category slug(s) for the game.

Hot.d: Listed on CrazyGames' 'hot' page when the snapshot was collected: the platform's own trending flag.

Untagged.d: Games of the row with no mechanic tag: the blind spot of the taxonomy.

Score.d: Opportunity score: Roblox heat and propagation, boosted by emergence, divided by the web supply already in place. A hypothesis to recalibrate once ~10 snapshots exist.
Score.f: (Roblox CCU/1000)^0.45 x (1 + 0.4 x min(IPs, 6)) x (1 + 0.5 x min(New <28d, 3)) / (1 + 0.6 x sqrt(Web supply))

Status.d: Verdict from fixed thresholds, checked in this order: absent (no game above the floor); supply unknown (a sitemap was missing); saturated (web supply >= 120); too small (Roblox CCU < 50,000); OPEN LANE (web supply = 0); emerging (New <28d >= 1 and supply <= 15); spreading (IPs >= 3 and supply <= 45); established otherwise.

Days.d: Elapsed time between the two snapshots compared, in days, from their collection timestamps (fractional: two runs 12 hours apart give 0.5). Every '/7d' figure is a raw difference multiplied by 7 / Days, so full and partial weeks compare.
Days.f: (collected_at_now - collected_at_prev) in days; 7 / Days is the scaling factor

Unity share.d: Share of the tracked CrazyGames games whose reported technology is Unity.
Unity share.f: count(tech contains 'unity') / count(tracked CrazyGames games with a known tech)

Web games.d: Web games in the row (catalogue supply).

Roblox games.d: Roblox games in the row (frame, above the floor).

Trend.d: Sparkline of the Score over every stored snapshot, oldest on the left. Flat with two points; it earns its place as weeks accumulate.
Trend.f: Score per snapshot, each computed against its baseline

Reading.d: One sentence generated from the lane's figures (players and their change, web supply and its change, concentration or creators, fresh releases) followed by the verdict that its Status implies. Every number in it is a column defined here.

Lane.d: Same as Mechanic: the game loop the site ranks. Used as the shorter word in headings.

Web arrivals.d: Web games matching the lane that entered the catalogue since the baseline.
Web arrivals.f: count of new catalogue slugs matched by the lane's web keywords, baseline to now

Confidence.d: How much the DATA behind a lane's reading can be trusted this week: four checks, each a fact with its threshold (baseline gap 6–8.5 days within 3 h of the same hour; both sitemaps read; 4+ snapshots over 21+ days; 3+ creators and no game above 60 %). A = 4 passed, B = 3, C = 2, D = 1 or 0. Not a probability of success.
Confidence.f: grade by count of checks passed; analysis.confidence

Saturation.d: Web supply of the lane against the saturated threshold, as a filled bar.

Opportunity.d: The lane's Score as a share of the best Score this snapshot, so lanes can be compared at a glance. The Score itself keeps its formula.

Day range.d: Lowest and highest reading of players online that day. The gap between the two is the daily cycle the day mean removes.
Day range.f: min and max of the day's readings

Readings.d: How many times players online were read that day: 1 without intraday samples, 3 when both samples ran.

Firing.d: How many signals of this rule fire in the current snapshot. A rule that fires on a third of the frame (accelerating game with a half-day baseline) is telling you about the baseline, not the market.
Firing.f: count of the rule's signals in the current snapshot

Hybrid.d: A game whose name matches the keywords of two lanes at once (Steal An Egg is steal-and-defend and pet-horde). Counted per pair of lanes, on Roblox over this week's frame and on the web over the whole catalogue: the chord between two lanes is as thick as the count.
Hybrid.f: count of games tagged with both lanes

Description.d: First 500 characters of the Roblox description, as stored.

Published.d: Publication date reported by the web platform (CrazyGames addedOn, Poki datePublished).

Signal.d: A rule-based leading indicator: a fact observed this snapshot that has historically preceded a move of a lane, before the ranking shows it. The rule of every signal is written next to it; its reliability is measured, never asserted (see Precision).

Rule.d: The exact condition that fires the signal, with its thresholds.

Value.d: The figure the rule was checked against for this signal (momentum, places gained, players, web supply, baseline rank).

Expected outcome.d: What the signal is supposed to precede: the lane's pooled Roblox CCU higher ('up') or lower ('down') at the first snapshot at least 28 days after the signal.

Precision.d: Share of past signals of that kind whose expected outcome happened, measured by replaying the archive. '-' until at least one signal is old enough to be judged; read it together with Cases.
Precision.f: hits / cases, cases = signals with a snapshot >= 28 days later

Cases.d: Number of past signals or projections old enough to be judged (a snapshot at least the horizon later exists).

Pending.d: Signals or projections too recent to be judged yet.

Phase.d: Lifecycle phase of a game from the trend of its last 14 daily points: launch (younger than 28 days), rising (at least +15 % a week), plateau, past peak (now at or below 80 % of the window's maximum), fading (at least -15 % a week). 'not enough history' under 8 points.
Phase.f: sign and size of the fitted daily growth of log(players); see the phase rules on the Projections page

Weekly trend.d: Fitted growth of players per week, from a least-squares line through log(players + 1) over the last 14 daily points.

+7d.d: Projected players 7 days after the snapshot: the fitted line extended, with a 90 % band from the spread of the fit's residuals (never narrower than +-5 %). Read the backtest before trusting it.
+7d.f: exp(a + b x (t + 7)) - 1, band = exp(+-1.645 x max(sigma, 0.05))

+14d.d: Projected players 14 days after the snapshot, same method as +7d.

+28d.d: Projected players 28 days after the snapshot, same method as +7d.

Points.d: Daily points used by the fit (at most 14).

Horizon.d: Days between a projection and the actual value it is scored against.

Direction hit rate.d: Share of past projections whose predicted direction (more or fewer players than on the day of the projection) matched what happened, measured by replaying the archive.

Median error.d: Median absolute error of the projected midpoint against the actual players at the horizon, as a share of the actual.

Band coverage.d: Share of actual values that fell inside the 90 % band. An honest band covers about 90 %; a lower figure means the bands are too narrow.

Hot since.d: First day of the lane's current run above the player floor (50,000 pooled CCU). 'before the archive' when it was already hot at the first snapshot; '-' when it is not hot now.

Arrivals.d: Web games matching the lane that entered the Poki or CrazyGames catalogue since the previous snapshot, summed over the whole archive, with the last 28 days in brackets.
Arrivals.f: count of new catalogue slugs matched by the lane's web keywords

Heat event.d: A day the lane crossed the player floor upward, or doubled its pooled players compared with 28 days earlier while above the floor. The clock of the lag starts here.

Web response.d: The first day, after a heat event, on which the lane has received at least 2 web arrivals since the event. '-' while it has not happened.

Heat events.d: Number of heat events observed for the lane in the archive.

Lag.d: Days between a heat event and its web response. 'pending (n days)' while no response has been observed; the number of days is how long the lane has stayed unserved so far.
Lag.f: web response date - heat event date

Best lag.d: Shift, in weeks, at which the lane's weekly Roblox players correlate best with its weekly web arrivals: the delay after which the web tends to follow. Shown only with at least 8 weekly points.
Best lag.f: argmax over k of corr(players[t], arrivals[t + k])

Correlation.d: Pearson correlation at the best lag, from -1 to 1. Near 0 means no visible link yet; read it with the number of weeks.

Weeks.d: Weekly points available for the correlation.

Created.d: Creation date of the universe as Roblox stores it (UTC).

Clone wave.d: Every stored game of a lane placed by its creation date, circle area = players online today. Reads whether the lane is an old genre, one hit, or a wave of copies in progress. Only games alive in the sorts today appear: a wave that died leaves no trace here.

Rank.d: Position in the ranking, 1 = the highest score.

Visits heat.d: The score with heat taken from visits gained instead of players online: (Visits/7d ÷ 7 ÷ 1000)^0.45 × the same three factors. Indifferent to the hour of collection. Shown as rank · score (change of rank against the current ranking).

Breadth heat.d: The score with heat taken from the lane's players WITHOUT its top game: the loop rather than the hit; a one-game lane scores 0. Shown as rank · score (change of rank).
Breadth heat.f: ((Roblox CCU − top game CCU) / 1000)^0.45 × the same factors

Live supply.d: The score with web supply reduced to its living share: supply × the share of tracked games that gained votes over the period (Votes/7d ≥ 1). Dash with fewer than 5 tracked games with a vote history. Shown as rank · score (change of rank).
Live supply.f: (Roblox CCU / 1000)^0.45 × the same factors / (1 + 0.6 × √(Web supply × alive share))

Rank agreement.d: Spearman rank correlation between the current ranking and a variant's, over the lanes where the variant exists: 1 = identical order, 0 = unrelated, negative = reversed.
Rank agreement.f: Pearson r of the two rank lists

Date.d: The day the snapshot was collected (UTC).

Collected at.d: Time of day (UTC) the full collection ran. The cron is 20:17 UTC; a run more than 3 h away reads the sorts of another moment of the day.

Day span.d: Hours between the first and the last reading of players online that day (intraday readings plus the snapshot's own). Below 6 h the day mean reads a narrow part of the daily cycle.
Day span.f: last reading - first reading, in hours

Frame.d: Universes shown in the four frame sorts that day: the sampling frame of every pooled Roblox figure. About 230 on a normal day.

Frame players.d: Players online summed over the frame at the snapshot's own reading (collection time, not the day mean).
Frame players.f: sum of playing over the frame universes at collection time

Catalogue.d: Games listed in each platform's sitemap that day, Poki then CrazyGames; 'fallback' when the sitemap was missing and the previous catalogue was used.

Pages read.d: Game pages read per platform that day, Poki then CrazyGames, with failed pages in brackets when any.

Requests.d: HTTP requests the run made, as counted by the collector (about 340 for a full run, a dozen for a reading); '-' for snapshots older than the counter.

Health.d: The day's verdict from the health checks of health.py: OK, WARN (usable, degraded or unusual) or FAIL (would poison the series; such a run is not committed unless forced). Each rule and its threshold is listed in the Health section.
Health.f: FAIL if any failing check, else WARN if any warning, else OK
